battle.name: 意大利戰爭 (1536年—1538年)
battle.theater: 普羅旺斯與皮埃蒙特戰線
battle.brief: 卡爾五世在義大利的地位到頂點，法王弗朗索瓦一世拒絕解散干邑聯盟，戰事隨即爆發。一五三六年帝國軍自米蘭越嶺攻入普羅旺斯，八月逼降馬賽；法國聯軍翌年六月在塞拉瓦萊擊潰帝國縱隊，救不了聯盟瓦解。一五三八年《尼斯和約》逼法國退出米蘭。全役火槍隊以火繩步槍為骨幹，輪發手槍只配軍官與近衛。

kit.name: 輪發手槍
kit.history: 最早的後膛手槍。機械太貴，只給火槍隊的軍官與近衛。

countries: 此役的交戰方是法王弗朗索瓦一世領頭的干邑聯盟，與哈布斯堡皇帝卡爾五世兩邊。聯盟方面，法國王室的常備軍與重騎自各地集結，樞密院與王室近親共同主導：波旁公爵查理三世以法國騎兵總帥之號執掌野戰軍隊，旺多姆伯爵尚·德·波旁·德·旺多姆則以王室身份坐鎮普羅旺斯，代表國王與地方貴族的雙重利益；威尼斯共和國出動本土傭兵與沿海船隊，由全軍總指揮與後勤總監分掌戰務與糧秣；教宗保羅三世以教宗國軍隊加入，他是促成聯盟的關鍵人物，卻自始把教宗國的安危置於聯盟勝負之前；熱那亞共和國在海上出力，但海軍首腦安德烈亞·多里亞的取向可以隨時左右戰局；米蘭公國由斯福爾扎家族掛名承襲，實際守城者與駐軍多受法國影響；曼圖亞、薩伏依與費拉拉等小邦，則在兩邊之間逐利。帝國方面，卡爾五世以西班牙老兵方陣為骨幹，混編德意志、義大利與那不勒斯的帝國部隊，由那不勒斯總督查理·德·拉努瓦以皇帝全權代表的身份統率全軍；薩伏依公爵埃馬努埃爾·菲利貝托站在皇帝一方，率領本國與皮埃蒙特的殘餘兵員。其正式編制是西班牙方陣，步兵按火槍手與長矛手的比例混編，砲兵以攻城重砲為主力。戰區之外的英格蘭與蘇格蘭一度靠向法國，蘇丹的奧斯曼帝國也與法國簽有針對哈布斯堡的默契，皇帝因此必須在歐洲與地中海兩線同時應付。
countriesEn: The two sides in this war were the League of Cognac under King Francis I of France, and the Habsburg emperor Charles V. On the League side the French royal army and its heavy cavalry were gathered from across the kingdom, with the privy council and the king's close relatives jointly directing them: Charles III of Bourbon commanded the field army as Constable of France, while Jean de Bourbon, Count of Vendôme, sat in Provence in the king's name, representing both the crown and the local nobles; the Republic of Venice sent mercenary foot and coastal squadrons, with a provveditore generale overseeing operations and a separate official handling supply and pay; Pope Paul III entered the league with the armies of the Papal States, and though he was the man who brought the league together he placed the safety of the Papal States ahead of the fortunes of the alliance at every turn; the Republic of Genoa contributed at sea, but the orientation of its admiral, Andrea Doria, could turn the balance at any moment; the Duchy of Milan was kept in name by the Sforza family, with Ottavio Farnese inheriting the name, while the garrison and the actual government in the city leaned towards France; Mantua, Savoy and Ferrara, small states, trimmed their sails to suit whoever was winning. On the imperial side Charles V built his army on Spanish tercios, mixing in German, Italian and Neapolitan troops, and gave the command to Charles de Lannoy, viceroy of Naples, acting as the emperor's plenipotentiary; Emmanuel Philibert, Duke of Savoy, stood with the emperor and led what was left of his own Savoyard and Piedmontese forces. The regular formation was the Spanish tercio, in which the foot were mixed in fixed proportions of arquebusiers and pikemen, with siege guns as the main weight of the artillery. Outside the theatre England and Scotland leaned towards France for a time, and the Ottoman sultan had a loose understanding with France aimed at the Habsburgs, which meant the emperor had to meet a war in Europe and another in the Mediterranean at the same time.
people: 全場的兩位主角是兩位君主。卡爾五世時年三十六歲，兼有西班牙王、哈布斯堡家系首領與神聖羅馬帝國皇帝三重身分，一五三〇年由教宗加冕為皇帝之後，一心要讓天主教世界恢復秩序；他不肯接受法國對米蘭的佔有，甚至放話要打到巴黎去。弗朗索瓦一世則是引信本身：他在帕維亞戰敗被俘、囚於西班牙三年，一五三六年一月才返國，隨即把重點放在收復米蘭，並在不肯輸掉任何一場歐洲大戰的傲氣之下拉起干邑聯盟。將領方面，法國一邊有旺多姆伯爵尚·德·波旁（馬賽的實際守將，屢次頂住帝國軍攻城）、波旁公爵查理三世（法國騎兵總帥）、昂古恩伯爵弗朗索瓦·德·波旁（一五三七年塞拉瓦萊之役的勝將），以及王弟阿朗松主持的樞密會議。帝國一邊有那不勒斯總督拉努瓦（全軍總指揮）、佩斯卡拉侯爵費蘭特·德·阿瓦洛斯與其弟費拉拉侯爵阿方索·德·阿瓦洛斯（兄長於一五三七年病逝後接掌兵權）、薩伏依公爵埃馬努埃爾·菲利貝托（綽號鐵頭），以及地中海海軍名將阿爾瓦羅·德·巴薩。教宗保羅三世與其姪法爾內塞紅衣主教是聯盟的樞紐；威尼斯方面由海陸總帥與後勤總監共同負責；熱那亞的安德烈亞·多里亞是最關鍵的變數，他先以熱那亞海軍替聯盟作戰，一五三八年卻轉向皇帝並交出艦隊，聯盟隨之瓦解。最後不能忘記人數最多的那一批：那幾萬名方陣步兵、幾千名火槍手、數千騎兵、砲手、水手與隨軍工匠。
peopleEn: The two principals of this war were two monarchs. Charles V was thirty-six and carried three titles at once — king of Spain, head of the Habsburg house and emperor of the Romans — and since his coronation by the pope in 1530 he had been bent on restoring order in the Catholic world; he would not accept France's occupation of Milan, and he talked openly of marching on Paris. Francis I was the fuse himself: he had been beaten and captured at Pavia and kept in Spain for three years, returning home only in January 1536, whereupon he made the recovery of Milan his object and, in a spirit of pride that would not concede a single great battle in Europe, assembled the League of Cognac. Among the commanders, the French side had Jean de Bourbon, Count of Vendôme, who was the actual defender of Marseille and repeatedly checked the imperial siege; Charles III of Bourbon, Constable of France, who led the French cavalry; François de Bourbon, Count of Enghien, who won the battle of Serravalle in 1537; and the council chaired by the king's brother Alençon. The imperial side had Lannoy, viceroy of Naples and commander in chief; Ferrante d'Avalos, Marquis of Pescara, and his brother Alfonso d'Avalos, Marquis del Vasto, who took over the command in 1537 after his elder brother's death; Emmanuel Philibert of Savoy, called the Ironhead; and the Mediterranean admiral Álvaro de Bazán. Pope Paul III and his nephew Cardinal Farnese were the hinges of the league; Venice left the conduct of the war to a general of the army and a provveditore for the logistics; and Andrea Doria of Genoa was the decisive variable, fighting the league's war first in the Genoese fleet and then going over to the emperor in 1538 and handing over his ships, with the league falling apart behind him. Last should come the largest body of participants: the tens of thousands of men in the tercios, the thousands of arquebusiers, the thousands of horsemen, the gunners, the sailors and the artificers on the march.
kits: 此役的裝備骨架是火繩步槍、長矛、火砲與騎兵火器四件套。西班牙方陣的火力核心是火繩手槍，射手以支架成排射擊，裝填慢、怕雨，但在十六世紀中葉仍是歐洲最靠得住的步槍；法國與聯盟一側同時推廣帶支架的輕型火繩步槍與初生的火繩火槍，火力密度未必遜於西班牙人。攻城方面，卡爾五世為一五三六年的普羅旺斯征伐在巴塞羅那特製了十二門巨砲「十二使徒」，口徑與重量都是當時歐洲之最，隨軍長途運到前線，正是它們在馬賽城牆上砸出缺口。卡面這件輪發手槍在此役的位置相當明確：它是十五世紀末到十六世紀初在低地國家與德意志出現的後膛機構，靠發條帶動的火鐧打火，不必用火繩，但每次上弦要轉動多圈，還得另帶上弦匙；機件脆、怕潮濕，火藥消耗大，價錢遠高於火繩手槍。因此西班牙方面只把它配給火槍隊的軍官、王室近衛與侍從，用途是近身自衛、騎戰中補上最後一擊，以及對付衝到面前的落馬騎士與散兵；再配一面小圓盾使用，是當時西班牙軍官與近衛的標準配置，也是卡面那句「機械太貴」的實情。帝國軍中的德意志與義大利傭兵則更多使用火繩手槍與長柄斧矛。騎兵方面，雙方都用長柄騎槍配火繩手槍的組合；海戰靠的是威尼斯與熱那亞的槳帆大艦，後膛手槍與火繩火砲在甲板與船樓的射擊同樣靠火繩。海運與糧秣是此役真正的短板：皇帝的大軍深入普羅旺斯之後，前線靠海路與陸路兩條補給線維持，一旦西班牙船隊與威尼斯艦隊在海上角力，遠征軍的糧草與攻城砲彈就都受制於海面。
kitsEn: The equipment skeleton of this war was a set of four: matchlock arquebus, pike, artillery and mounted firearms. The heart of the Spanish tercio's firepower was the matchlock arquebus, fired by ranks of shooters working off their rests; slow to load and afraid of rain, it was still the most dependable musket in Europe in the middle of the sixteenth century, and on the French and League side a light matchlock arquebus on a rest and the newly appearing matchlock musket were being pushed forward, so that the density of fire was by no means inferior to the Spanish. On the siege side, Charles V had twelve great guns cast in Barcelona for his Provençal campaign of 1536, the Twelve Apostles, whose calibre and weight were the greatest in Europe, and they were hauled a long way to the front, and it was they that opened a breach in the walls of Marseille. The position of the wheel-lock pistol on this card in this war is quite exact: it is the rear-locking mechanism that appeared in the Low Countries and in Germany at the close of the fifteenth and the opening of the sixteenth century, fired by a spring-driven frizzen instead of a match, but slow to cock through many turns and requiring a separate key to be carried on the person; the mechanism is fragile, it is hurt by damp, it drinks powder, and it costs many times the price of a matchlock pistol. Spain therefore issued it only to the officers of the firearm companies, to the royal guard and to the personal attendants, for close self-defence, for the last shot of a mounted action, and for shooting unhorsed riders and stragglers who came close; carried with a small round shield, it was the standard kit of the Spanish officer and of the guard, and that is the plain sense of the card's remark that the mechanism was too expensive. The German and Italian mercenaries in the imperial army used matchlock pistols and long-handled axes far more. The cavalry on both sides used the long lance with the matchlock pistol; the sea war was fought in the galleys of Venice and Genoa, where the wheel-lock pistol and the matchlock gun on deck and in the fighting tops were served with matches as well. Sea power and supply were the real weak point of this campaign: once the emperor's army was deep into Provence the front was held by two lines of supply, by sea and by land, and the moment the Spanish squadrons and the Venetian fleet jockeyed for position the food and the siege ammunition of the invading army were at the mercy of the water.
tactics: 卡爾五世對法國的計劃是兩路進攻：自米蘭與自北面各出一軍，企圖讓法國腹背受敵。一五三六年春，帝國主力自米蘭越過阿爾卑斯山進入普羅旺斯，進逼馬賽，圍城自初夏打到八月，攻城重砲與雲梯同時使用，城內糧盡，馬賽在八月十二日開城，聖尼古拉堡壘仍死守到十一月四日才降。聯盟的戰法是把海陸兩種力量合起來用：威尼斯艦隊在海上牽制帝國航路，聯盟陸軍則在皮埃蒙特與米蘭一線包抄。一五三七年六月二日的塞拉瓦萊之戰是全役最典型的一次戰術示範：法國與薩伏依的聯軍在塞拉瓦萊河谷撞上正在行軍的帝國縱隊，沒有正面硬撞，而是以騎兵迂迴側翼、步兵與砲兵在正面釘住，帝國縱隊被拉成數段，砲兵與輜重車隊首尾不能相顧，撤退時又在渡河處被截斷而崩潰，帝國軍的砲隊與大批裝備成了繳獲。法國騎兵在此役仍偏重偵察、追擊與襲擾糧道，真正決定會戰的仍是步兵火力的密度與砲兵展開的位置；塞拉瓦萊的教訓被西班牙方陣記取，此後縱隊行軍加強了前哨與側翼警戒。帝國一方的攻城有一套成熟辦法：壕溝、鹿砦與配屬火砲把野戰兵變成攻城兵，一五三八年聯盟圍攻尼斯時，雙方在城下的對峙就照這套辦法進行。聯盟的崩解同樣有戰術層面的原因：熱那亞海軍倒向皇帝、威尼斯選擇保存實力、教宗國既要聯盟又要單獨媾和，前線兵力被逐漸抽走，攻勢變成待援，最終在《尼斯和約》簽訂時全線停火。
tacticsEn: Charles V's plan against France was a two-pronged invasion, one army out of Milan and another from the north, so as to turn France front and rear. In the spring of 1536 the imperial main army crossed the Alps out of Milan into Provence and drove on Marseille; the siege ran from early summer to August, siege guns and ladders in use together, the city out of food, Marseille opening its gates on the twelfth of August, while the citadel of Saint-Nicolas held out until the fourth of November before it surrendered. The League's method was to combine sea power and land power: the Venetian fleet held the imperial sea route in check while the allied armies worked round the Piedmontese and Milanese line. The battle of Serravalle on 2 June 1537 is the clearest tactical lesson of the whole campaign: the French and Savoyard allies ran into an imperial column on the march in the valley of the Scrivia and did not strike it head on, but turned their cavalry around the flank and pinned the front with infantry and guns, so that the column was stretched into several segments, the artillery and the baggage train could not see one another, and the retreat was cut at the crossing and turned into a rout, the imperial guns and a great part of the equipment becoming booty. The French cavalry in this war still leaned towards scouting, pursuit and raiding the supply line, and what really decided the engagement was still the density of infantry fire and the position from which the guns were deployed; the lesson of Serravalle was taken to heart by the Spanish tercios, and columns on the march afterwards kept sharper outposts and covered flanks. The imperial side had a mature method for siege: the ditch, the redoubt and the attached guns turned field soldiers into siege troops, and that is how the two sides lay opposite one another before Nice in 1538. The League's collapse had tactical reasons as well: the Genoese navy went over to the emperor, Venice chose to husband its strength, the Papal States wanted the league and a separate peace at the same time, troops were drawn off the front line by degrees, the offensive changed into a wait for relief, and the whole line went quiet when the Peace of Nice was signed.
data: 有根據的數字集中在幾個節點上。一五三六年，帝國軍自米蘭越過阿爾卑斯山，兵力以數萬計，馬賽守軍約六千人，圍城自初夏延至八月十二日，堡壘則守到十一月四日；一五三七年六月二日的塞拉瓦萊之戰，帝國與西班牙方面的兵力在史家記載中自一萬上下至一萬二千人不等，法國與薩伏依聯軍的數目不到其半；同年聯軍曾包圍米蘭城，帝國總督烏戈·德·卡爾多納苦守，數月之後由皇帝解圍。攻城重砲方面，「十二使徒」共十二門，是一五三五年在巴塞羅那特製的巨砲群，重量以噸計，裝藥量與射程都遠超野戰砲。一五三八年六月二十一日《尼斯和約》的主要數字是：法國放棄米蘭，支付五萬埃居作為補償，並約定把王太子亨利送往西班牙作人質；卡爾五世則放棄對勃艮第的索求，承認法國王位，聯盟解散，作為交換取得皇帝在義大利的絕對優勢與對抗奧斯曼的自由。背景數字也可一併記下：一五二六年《馬德里條約》規定法國以二百萬埃居贖回弗朗索瓦一世，這筆錢的規模說明哈布斯堡握有什麼樣的談判籌碼；一五三八年九月皇帝轉向地中海，同年九月二十九日的海雷戰役中，帝國海軍敗於蘇萊曼的海軍，說明和約換來的不是戰爭的結束，而是另一場戰爭的開始。傷亡方面，古文獻留下的數字多有誇大與互相矛盾之處，能確定的是雙方都有數千人的死傷與被俘，塞拉瓦萊一役帝國軍損失尤為慘重，傷者與散兵在撤往皮亞琴察的路上被大量遺棄；至於精確的陣亡人數，現有史料無法支持任何一個精確數字。
dataEn: The grounded figures cluster around a few fixed points. In 1536 the imperial army crossed the Alps out of Milan with a force of some tens of thousands; the garrison of Marseille was about six thousand men; the siege ran from early summer to the twelfth of August, and the citadel held on until the fourth of November. At the battle of Serravalle on 2 June 1537 the imperial and Spanish force is given in the sources as anywhere from ten thousand up to twelve thousand, while the French and Savoyard allies were less than half that number; in the same year the allies besieged the city of Milan, where the imperial governor Ugo de Cardona held out, and the emperor came to relieve the city after several months. On the artillery side, the Twelve Apostles were twelve great guns cast in Barcelona in 1535, weighing tons, with a charge and a range far beyond that of field pieces. The principal figures of the Peace of Nice of 21 June 1538 are these: France gave up Milan, paid fifty thousand écus in compensation, and agreed to send the Dauphin Henry to Spain as a hostage; Charles V in return dropped his claim to Burgundy, recognised the crown of France, and saw the League dissolved, receiving in exchange untrammelled predominance in Italy and a free hand against the Ottomans. The background figures can be set down as well: the Treaty of Madrid of 1526 laid down two million écus as the price of releasing Francis I, a sum whose size shows what leverage the Habsburgs held; and in September 1538, with the emperor turned toward the Mediterranean, the imperial fleet was beaten by the fleet of Suleiman in the battle of Preveza on the twenty-ninth of September, which shows that the treaty had not ended the war but begun another. On losses the numbers in the older narratives are inflated and contradict one another; what can be established is that both sides lost and took thousands of dead and prisoners, and that the imperial army suffered severely at Serravalle, where the wounded and the stragglers were abandoned in large numbers on the road to Piacenza; as for exact casualty figures, the surviving sources will not support any exact number at all.
cause: 導火線是一五二五年帕維亞之敗留下的舊賬。一五二五年九月二十五日，弗朗索瓦一世在帕維亞被卡爾五世的帝國軍與西班牙軍隊生擒，法軍幾乎全滅，他本人成了階下囚；一五二六年《馬德里條約》要求他放棄米蘭與勃艮第，支付二百萬埃居，並以他的兩個兒子作人質。弗朗索瓦在西班牙被囚三年，一五三六年一月才獲釋返法，此時的形勢對他並不有利：卡爾五世已於一五三〇年加冕為皇帝，帝國境內又面對著土耳其的壓力，卻仍握有米蘭、那不勒斯與西班牙的稅收，而法國在北義大利的立足點只剩下被聯盟包圍的一個米蘭。弗朗索瓦拒絕履行《馬德里條約》關於米蘭的讓步，他知道只要米蘭還在法國或法國盟國的手上，哈布斯堡在義大利的權力就永遠不完整；於是他在一五三六年六月拉起干邑聯盟，把威尼斯、教宗國、熱那亞、米蘭與若干小邦綁在同一張合約上，這個聯盟同時也是對卡爾五世在帝國境內擴張的直接挑戰。卡爾五世的反應是把聯盟視為必須先摧毀的陰謀：一五三六年他自米蘭出兵深入普羅旺斯，打算先拿下法國的大海門戶馬賽，切斷法國南方的糧源，再回師收拾聯盟。戰爭因此從一場義大利的爭端，變成從阿爾卑斯山打到地中海的全面對抗。
causeEn: The trigger was the old account left over from the defeat at Pavia in 1525. On 25 September 1525 Francis I was taken prisoner at Pavia by the imperial and Spanish forces of Charles V, the French army was practically annihilated, and the king himself became a captive; the Treaty of Madrid of 1526 required him to renounce Milan and Burgundy, to pay two million écus, and to give his two sons as hostages. Francis was held in Spain for three years and returned home only in January 1536, and the position was by no means favourable to him then: Charles V had been crowned emperor in 1530, the empire was under pressure from the Turks, and yet he still held Milan, Naples and the taxes of Spain, while the French foothold in northern Italy had shrunk to a single besieged Milan. Francis refused the cession of Milan laid down in the Treaty of Madrid, for he understood that as long as Milan remained in French or in allied hands the Habsburg power in Italy could never be complete; and so in June 1536 he drew up the League of Cognac, binding Venice, the Papal States, Genoa, Milan and a number of small states under one instrument, which was at the same time a direct challenge to Charles V's expansion inside the empire. Charles V's answer was to treat the league as a conspiracy that had to be destroyed first: in 1536 he marched out of Milan deep into Provence with the intention of taking Marseille, the great seaward door of France, cutting the food supply of the south, and only then turning back to settle with the league. The war thus turned from a quarrel over Italy into a general confrontation carried from the Alps to the Mediterranean.
impact: 此役的影響遠比它的戰果更深。第一，歐洲兩大國家第一次在義大利以外的地方、在法國本土上互相開火，戰爭的地理範圍被推開，替後來綿延到一五五九年的哈布斯堡-瓦洛瓦戰爭定了調子；此後法國每每要用西班牙的干預來對付自己的宗教異議，這條因果鏈的源頭正是一五三六年的干邑聯盟。第二，卡爾五世在《尼斯和約》之後得到他想要的東西：法國放棄米蘭，承認皇帝在義大利的權力，聯盟解散，維也納、威尼斯與教宗國各自回到服從的位置；帝國可以把注意力轉向奧斯曼，同年九月就爆發海雷戰役。義大利此後數十年落在西班牙的護盾之下，奧塔維奧·法爾內塞成為帝國承認的米蘭公爵，佛羅倫薩、威尼斯與教宗國在帝國的陰影下各取所需。第三，聯盟瓦解的方式留下了外交上的教訓：多里亞在最後關頭倒向皇帝，維也納選擇保存實力，聯盟在軍事上從未真正協同，只靠共同敵人維繫；此後歐洲的同盟常常在同樣的裂縫上散掉。第四，軍事技術上，此役是西班牙方陣制度成熟的標誌：火槍手的密集射擊、「十二使徒」這類巨型攻城砲的長距離調度，以及騎兵與步兵配合的追擊方式，都在此役裡被完整演練了一次；而卡面這件輪發手槍，也正是在這一時期由西班牙的工匠制度化，讓它從德意志傭兵營裡的貴重玩物，變成方陣中軍官與近衛的制式配備，之後才隨西班牙的銀流走向歐洲各處。第五，這場戰事拖住了皇帝西進的時間表，北非與地中海的計畫一推再推，歐洲因此多出一段喘息的窗口。
impactEn: The effects of this war ran far deeper than its results. First, for the first time the two great powers of Europe fired on each other outside Italy, on French soil, and the geography of European war was pushed open; the long Habsburg-Valois conflict that ran on to 1559 took its tone from here, and the habit of France calling in Spanish intervention against its own religious dissidents traces straight back to the League of Cognac of 1536. Second, after the Peace of Nice Charles V had what he wanted: France gave up Milan and acknowledged imperial authority in Italy, the league was dissolved, and Vienna, Venice and the Papal States each went back to a posture of obedience; the empire could turn its attention to the Ottomans, and in September of the same year the battle of Preveza followed. Italy lay for the next several decades under the Spanish shield, Ottavio Farnese became the duke of Milan recognised by the empire, and Florence, Venice and the Papal States each took what they could from the emperor's shadow. Third, the way the league fell apart left a diplomatic lesson: Doria turned to the emperor at the last moment, Venice chose to husband its strength, and the league was never coordinated in any military sense, being held together only by a common enemy; European alliances have often come apart along the same crack since. Fourth, in military terms this campaign marked the maturing of the Spanish tercio system: the dense fire of the arquebusiers, the long-range movement of enormous siege guns like the Twelve Apostles, and the pursuit by cavalry in concert with foot were all rehearsed here in full; and the wheel-lock pistol on this card was precisely in this period institutionalised by Spanish workmanship, changing from a costly curio of the German mercenary camps into the standard kit of officers and guards in the tercio, from which it later travelled with Spanish silver across Europe. Fifth, the war held up the emperor's timetable in the west, pushing back his plans for North Africa and the Mediterranean, and gave Europe a further window to breathe.
result: 一五三六年夏秋，帝國軍越過阿爾卑斯山攻入普羅旺斯，圍困馬賽，攻城砲在牆上砸出缺口，守軍糧盡，馬賽城於八月十二日開門投降，聖尼古拉堡壘繼續抵抗到十一月四日才掛旗。皇帝沒有就此罷手，卻也沒有一舉攻下法國：聯盟的陸軍與艦隊在南部牽制住帝國的分兵，佛羅倫薩與米蘭一線的聯軍於一五三七年包圍米蘭，帝國總督卡爾多納苦守待援。一五三七年六月二日，塞拉瓦萊的轉折出現了：法國與薩伏依的聯軍在河谷中突然截住帝國縱隊，迂迴側翼、斷其砲隊，帝國軍在撤退中被擊潰，裝備與火砲盡為敵所得，拉努瓦受傷，佩斯卡拉侯爵費蘭特·阿瓦洛斯同年病逝於米蘭，繼任的阿方索接掌指揮。這一仗讓聯盟在歐洲一度聲威大振，卻沒有改變聯盟的結構性弱點：威尼斯不願把海陸兵力押在一次會戰上，教宗保羅三世擔心教宗國在皇帝攻擊之下無險可守，熱那亞的多里亞則在皇帝的許諾下倒戈。一五三八年，聯盟圍攻尼斯，圍城自春延至夏；皇帝的海軍在地中海取得優勢，法國與聯盟的艦隊退守，尼斯始終未能攻下，圍城因和約而解。六月二十一日《尼斯和約》簽訂：法國放棄米蘭、支付五萬埃居、約定把王太子亨利送往西班牙作人質，聯盟解散，勃艮第問題擱置，皇帝取得在義大利的完全主導權，並得以轉向東方的奧斯曼。雙方都沒有毀掉對方：法國保住了本土，帝國保住了米蘭與義大利的秩序；這場戰爭沒有真正的勝負者，只有聯盟的解散與下一輪歐洲格局的鋪陳。
resultEn: In the summer and autumn of 1536 the imperial army crossed the Alps into Provence and invested Marseille; the siege guns opened a breach in the walls, the garrison ran out of food, and the city opened its gates on the twelfth of August, while the citadel of Saint-Nicolas went on resisting until the fourth of November. The emperor did not stop there, and yet he did not break France either: the allied armies and fleets held Imperial detachments in the south, and the League besieged Milan in 1537, where the imperial governor Cardona held out and waited for relief. The turning point came at Serravalle on 2 June 1537: the French and Savoyard allies cut the imperial column in the valley, turned its flank and destroyed its guns, and the imperial army was routed in its retreat, its equipment and artillery becoming booty; Lannoy was wounded, and the Marquis of Pescara, Ferrante d'Avalos, died of illness in Milan in the same year, his brother Alfonso taking over the command. That victory gave the League a moment of renown in Europe, but it changed none of the alliance's structural weaknesses: Venice would not stake its land and sea forces on a single engagement, Pope Paul III feared for the safety of the Papal States if the emperor turned on them, and Andrea Doria went over to the emperor on his promises. In 1538 the League besieged Nice; the siege ran from spring into summer, the emperor's fleet gained the upper hand in the Mediterranean, the French and allied squadrons withdrew, and Nice was never taken, the siege being dissolved by a treaty. On 21 June the Peace of Nice was signed: France gave up Milan, paid fifty thousand écus, and agreed to send the Dauphin Henry to Spain as a hostage; the league was dissolved, the Burgundian question was set aside, the emperor obtained complete predominance in Italy and was free to turn toward the Ottomans in the east. Neither side destroyed the other: France saved its own territory, the empire saved Milan and the order of Italy; this war had no real victor, only the dissolution of the League and the laying of the ground for the next European alignment.
